children: Denmark’s central bank increased its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.10% in September, following a similar move by the European Central Bank.
The ECB raised rates for the second time this year, saying the conflict in the Middle East continues to fuel inflationary pressures.
The decision ensures that the interest rate difference between Denmark and the Eurozone remains unchanged, maintaining the stability of Denmark's currency, the krone, against the euro.

Denmark's benchmark current account interest rate and the certificate of deposit rate were each hiked by 25 basis points to 2.10% from 2.25%, while the so-called lending rate was cut by 25 basis points to 2.50% from 2.75%.

title: Denmark Central Bank Follows ECB Rate Hike
